name: Les Mills Instructor App
tagline: The app certified Les Mills instructors use to get quarterly release choreography, music and training videos for programs like BodyPump and BodyCombat.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The app itself is a video player with a download manager and a program picker, which an agent could reproduce before lunch. The thing you are actually paying for is licensed choreography and licensed music for a specific quarterly release, plus the certification pipeline that gates access to it. You cannot build choreography you do not have, and you very much cannot build the music rights that let you play those tracks in a paid class. Any personal replacement is a shell with nothing legal to put in it. The honest consolation is a tool for your own classes: your own tracks, your own cues, your own timing.
coreLoopDIY: A local, offline class-prep app where you build your own track-by-track class plans with cues, timings and notes, and run them from a big-button stage view during class.
requirements: Music you actually have the right to use in class
Your own choreography notes, typed in by you
A phone browser for the stage view, or a laptop at the front of the room
whatYouLose: The actual quarterly release choreography, which is the entire product
Licensed music cleared for commercial class use
Masterclass and technique videos filmed with the program directors
Proof-of-training and certification tracking tied to your instructor record
Everything syncing to the club and to other instructors teaching the same release
moatNotes: Music licensing for group fitness is a real legal apparatus, not a feature flag. Les Mills sits between the labels, the clubs and the instructors, and that position is the business.
whyPeopleStillPay: Instructors pay because the choreography, the music and the right to teach the branded class are one bundle, and the app is just the delivery pipe. A club hires you to teach BodyPump 135, not your personal interpretation of it, so you need the real release and the real tracks on the day it drops. The subscription is closer to a licensing fee than to software, and nobody has ever churned off a fitness app because the video player was mediocre.
notes: The player is a weekend build; the release is not. The moat is music licensing plus the certification pipeline that decides who is allowed to teach the choreography at all.
prompt:
Build a local-first class prep and stage-view app for a fitness instructor. This is NOT a Les Mills client: it ships with no choreography and no music. It is a place to write down and run your own classes.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage
- vite-plugin-pwa so it installs on a phone and works fully offline
- No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no network calls at all

Data model:
- Class: name, format label, duration target, notes, createdAt
- Track: belongs to a Class, order index, title, artist, purpose label (warmup, squats, chest, core, cooldown, free text), durationSeconds, cue list
- Cue: timestampSeconds, text, intensity tag (low, build, peak)
- TaughtLog: classId, date, venue, headcount, free-text reflection

Screens:
1. Class list: cards with name, total runtime summed from tracks, last taught date. Create, duplicate, delete.
2. Class editor: drag-to-reorder tracks, inline edit of all fields, cue editor per track where you type a timestamp like 1:45 and a cue line.
3. Stage view: full screen, very large type, high contrast, black background. Shows current track title, purpose, a running timer, and the next cue highlighted as the timer passes its timestamp. Tap anywhere to advance to the next track. Keeps the screen awake using the Wake Lock API where available.
4. History: list of TaughtLogs with a simple count of how many times each class has been run.

Also build:
- Export and import the whole database as a single JSON file, with a file picker. This is the only backup mechanism.
- A seed button that creates one example class with three tracks and a few cues so the UI is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope: audio playback, music files, streaming, any bundled choreography, any sync, any sharing, any login. If you are tempted to add a login, do not.

No .env is needed because there are no secrets. Write a README that says plainly: this stores everything in your browser, clearing site data deletes your classes, use the JSON export.
